Attention updates a representation by combining information from selected source representations.
To identify its inputs, first identify the positions being updated and the positions they can read.
A token can represent a word, an image patch, a robot state, or an action position; its semantic type does not permanently assign it the role of query, key, or value.

Start with the [representation overview](representations.qmd) for the distinction between a sequence element and its numerical vector.

## Tokens and learned projections {#projections}

A token at a Transformer layer is represented by a vector.
The initial vector may come from a vocabulary embedding, an image encoder, a numerical projection, or a positional representation.
Later layers operate on the hidden representations produced by earlier computation.

For one attention head, let $X_q\in\mathbb R^{n_q\times d}$ contain the representations being updated and $X_s\in\mathbb R^{n_s\times d}$ contain the source representations.
For simplicity, both streams have input width $d$ here.
Attention forms

$$
  \begin{aligned}
  Q&=X_qW_Q,\\
  K&=X_sW_K,\\
  V&=X_sW_V.
  \end{aligned}
$$

The projection matrices are learned parameters.
The resulting $Q$, $K$, and $V$ are activations that change with the current input and layer.

| Object | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $Q$ | $n_q\times d_k$ | One query for each position being updated. |
| $K$ | $n_s\times d_k$ | One key for each source position. |
| $V$ | $n_s\times d_v$ | One value for each source position. |
| $QK^\top$ | $n_q\times n_s$ | A score for each query–source pair. |
| Output | $n_q\times d_v$ | One combined value vector per query. |

Architectures with different stream widths use compatible stream-specific projections.
A projection shared across positions does not mean the positions have identical activations.
The basic construction follows [Attention Is All You Need, Section 3.2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762).

## Scores, weights, and outputs {#weights-and-values}

For scaled dot-product attention,

$$
  S=\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}+M,
$$

$$
  P=\operatorname{softmax}_{\mathrm{row}}(S),
  \qquad Z=PV.
$$

Here, $M$ is an attention mask expressed as additive score adjustments.
The [mask section](#mask-values) specifies allowed and prohibited reads and the condition for a valid row.

The score $S_{ij}$ measures compatibility between query $i$ and source key $j$.
The weight $P_{ij}$ is nonnegative, and each row sums to one.
The output row is

$$
  Z_i=\sum_{j=1}^{n_s}P_{ij}V_j.
$$

The weights describe how information is combined; they are not the combined information itself.
The values provide that information.
Neither a query nor an attention output is automatically an action command: subsequent layers and an output projection determine what the model predicts.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false" title="Worked example: one query reading two values"}

Suppose one query produces weights $0.25$ and $0.75$.
Let the source values be $V_1=(2,0)$ and $V_2=(0,4)$.
Then

$$
  \begin{aligned}
  Z_1&=0.25(2,0)+0.75(0,4)\\
     &=(0.5,3).
  \end{aligned}
$$

There are two source positions but only one query, so this head produces one output vector.
Changing the number of source tokens changes the number of possible contributions, not the number of output positions.

:::

Multi-head attention performs several such combinations with separate learned projections.
It concatenates their outputs and applies an output projection.
A Transformer block also contains residual connections, normalisation, and a feed-forward component; attention is one operation within that block.

## Self-attention and cross-attention {#self-and-cross}

In self-attention, query and source representations come from the same sequence.
Every participating position supplies query, key, and value projections, subject to the mask.
In cross-attention, queries come from the sequence being updated and keys/values come from another sequence.

For example, a decoder can contain $H$ action positions and read $N$ encoded observation positions.
Its cross-attention scores have shape $H\times N$.
It produces $H$ updated representations, one per action position, even when $H\ne N$.

The source and destination matter more than the words “encoder” and “decoder.”
An encoder can use self-attention, and a decoder can use both self-attention and cross-attention.
[Section 3.2.3 of the Transformer paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) identifies these roles for the original encoder–decoder architecture.

## Causal and block attention masks {#mask-values}

An attention mask controls forward access: it determines which source positions a query can use.
A causal mask prevents a position from reading prohibited future positions.
A block mask can allow an action stream to read a prefix while preventing the prefix from reading actions.

The additive mask has one entry per query–source pair:

$$
  M_{ij}=
  \begin{cases}
    0,&\text{if the read is allowed},\\
    -\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
$$

A prohibited pair then receives zero softmax weight.
Every query must retain at least one allowed source; a row containing only prohibited scores does not define a valid attention distribution.

## Forward Access and Gradient Paths {#masks-and-gradients}

A mask excludes prohibited query–source pairs from this attention operation.
[Stop-gradient](../computer-software/stop-gradient.qmd) preserves a forward value but blocks derivatives through a specified computation edge.
An action stream can therefore read a prefix through detached keys and values: the information is available even though that path cannot update its producer.
[Knowledge insulation](../../literature-review/action/knowledge-insulation.qmd) relies on this distinction.

## Attention order does not determine generation order {#generation-order}

A causal attention mask specifies dependencies inside a network evaluation.
Autoregressive generation additionally feeds generated outputs back as inputs for later output positions.
A denoising network can use causal attention over noisy action positions while updating a whole candidate chunk in one evaluation.

To decide whether a policy is autoregressive, inspect its generation loop and predicted object.
[Generative action models](generative-models.qmd#taxonomy) separates architecture, objective, and sampling order.

## Action positions before actions have been predicted {#action-positions}

A decoder can allocate a representation for each future action position before it knows the action's numerical value.
The representation says which output position is being formed.
It need not be a previously predicted command.

In [ACT](../../literature-review/action/act.qmd), decoder positions read encoded observation and latent information to produce the whole action chunk.
The paper describes fixed sinusoidal positional inputs; the released implementation uses learned query embeddings.
Those are different constructions of the initial slot representations, while the attention projections are learned in either case.
The ACT review records the source distinction.

A query coming from an action position therefore does not imply that a clean future action was supplied at inference.
For diffusion or flow policies, an action position can instead start with an embedding of its current noisy numerical value.
That noisy candidate is an available input even though the clean target is unknown.

## Robot state and attention Q are different objects {#robot-state}

Robotics papers often write $q_t$ for current joint positions or proprioceptive measurements.
Attention papers write $Q$ for query activations.
The similar letters do not imply that all attention queries come from robot state.

For an action token with hidden representation $h_a$, its query is formed from that token:

$$
  Q_a=h_aW_Q^a.
$$

It can read keys and values from permitted image, text, state, or action tokens.
The precise set depends on the architecture and mask.

~~~{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["Current action representation"] --> Q["Action query"]
  C["Permitted context representations"] --> K["Context keys"]
  C --> V["Context values"]
  Q --> S["Scores and attention weights"]
  K --> S
  S --> Z["Updated action representation"]
  V --> Z
~~~

This diagram shows information flow for one action query, not a complete model architecture.
Other action tokens can be additional sources if the mask permits them.
In [π0](../../literature-review/action/pi0.qmd) and [π0.5](../../literature-review/action/pi05.qmd), also check where state is represented before deciding which stream owns its projections.

## Connections {#connections}

[Stop-gradient](../computer-software/stop-gradient.qmd) controls where a loss can send derivatives while leaving a forward value readable.
[KV caching](kv-cache.qmd) reuses keys and values when the mask and inputs keep their representations independent of newly added or changing inputs.
[BERT](../../literature-review/language/bert.qmd) and [PaliGemma](../../literature-review/multimodality/paligemma.qmd) illustrate different bidirectional and causal access patterns.
